text:
Jordan: Heads-up — seeing a spike in stale SSE handles when clients 'pause' then come back. They never fully resume and stay in the routing table.
Mira: repro steps?
Jordan: Repro: lightweight mobile emulator opens SSE, sends tiny keepalive every 25s, then we simulate a network pause for ~70s, resume; server returns a 204 and closes.
Kevin: Is this after the keepalive tweak from last week?
Jordan: yes. We moved the pause-window timeout to 60s. Looks like tombstone TTL < client pause so router gives up early.
Mira: Console shows a micro-spike at 13:37 UTC and the stale_streams alert fired, but the route cleanup metric didn't drop.
ops-bot: Incident created: IN-2026-113 — stale SSE handles on edge nodes
Jordan: Quick log excerpt:```
edge: conn_id=abcd state=paused last_msg=2026-03-19T13:36:12Z ttl=60
router: lease_expiry=2026-03-19T13:37:12Z tombstone=false
```
Mira: my hunch: pause-window backoff race with resubscribe path — we cancel the connection earlier but the resume path expects KV cache still valid.
Kevin: Two routes: bump tombstone TTL to 90s (fast mitigation) OR make resume idempotent to accept late frames (long-term).
Mira: Prefer idempotent resume + better tracing. Increasing TTL just masks the root issue.
Jordan: Also need console telemetry: pause counts per client type, resume-latency histogram, and flag when resume falls back to long-polling. Right now it's opaque.
Kevin: I'll add metrics sse.pause_window_ms and sse.resume_latency_ms and a boolean sse.resume_fallback. Will wire heatmap in console.
Mira: can we tag traces with client_user_agent so we can filter thin clients (flutter/emulator) vs full browsers?
Jordan: yes — add tag user_agent:flutter_emulator and user_agent:chrome.
Kevin: rolling a tiny change to canary now. Will push patch + e2e harness.
deploy-bot: started canary deploy for platform/streaming@v2.18.3
Mira: After canary, please run the flutter emulator synthetic test (the one that pauses network for 70s).
Jordan: ack. If synthetic shows reduced stale entries we can promote.
Mira: FYI noticed a secondary effect: when many paused streams resume at once, proxy returns 429s and some resumes drop. Might be a resume-flood problem.
Jordan: that explains the 204 close + missing resume. Quota throttle fires on resume flood.
Kevin: plan: per-tenant resume queue with small jitter + exponential backoff on 429. Should smooth the spike.
Mira: owners: Kevin (implementation), Jordan (synthetic), Mira (console + alerts). I'll update the playbook with steps to run the harness and how to validate the heatmap.
Jordan: adding unit tests for resume idempotency and integration test in streaming-sim to exercise pause/resume windows.
Mira: small UX note — console should show both current active count and "paused but healthy" count so oncall can tell if it's a transient pause vs teardown.
Kevin: good call. I'll add that tile.
Jordan: thanks everyone. Will post follow-ups after canary completes.
Mira: :thumbsup:
